title: "Mini-Project #02: Identifying Environmentally Responsible US Public Transit Systems"
author: "Mahisa Alam"

## Introduction

The objective of this project is to assess the environmental impact of the transit agencies in the United States and find out which agency performs better in terms of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. To conduct this assessment, this project uses the information collected from the National Transit Database and the Energy Information Administration regarding the usage of energy in the transit systems, number of riders and the greenhouse gas emissions from electricity generation at the state level. This data is then compared to calculate the emissions generated by the transit system and the emissions that would have been generated if the riders took private cars instead.

## Data Acquisition

### State Electricity Profiles
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(rvest)

get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
    library(tidyverse)
    library(stringr)
    library(httr2)
    library(rvest)
    library(fs)
  
    state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")
    
    dir_name <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
    file_name <- fs::path(dir_name, state_formatted)
    
    fs::dir_create(dir_name, recurse=TRUE)
    
    if(!fs::file_exists(file_name)){
        BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"
        RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |> 
          req_url_path("electricity", 
                       "state", 
                       state_formatted) |>
          req_headers(
            `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
            ) |>   
          req_retry(
                max_tries = 4, 
          ) |>
          req_perform(file_name)
    
        resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
    }
    
    TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |> 
        html_element("table") |> 
        html_table() |>
        mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))
    
    if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
        TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
    }
    
    CO2_MWh <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |> 
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    PRIMARY <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> 
        pull(Rank)
    
    RATE <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        as.numeric()
    
    GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    data.frame(CO2_MWh               = CO2_MWh, 
               primary_source        = PRIMARY,
               electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10, # / 100 cents to dollars &
               # * 1000 kWh to MWH 
               generation_MWh        = GENERATION_MWh, 
               state                 = state, 
               abbreviation          = abbr
    )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()
```

### NTD Energy Consumption
```{r}
load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/") |>
      req_url_path("sites",
                   "fta.dot.gov",
                   "files",
                   "2026-09",
                   "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx") |> 
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_energy.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()
```

### NTD Transit Service
```{r}
load_ntd_service <- function(){
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query`=paste(
        "SELECT  `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`", 
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000", 
        sep=",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate))
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()
```

## Exploratory Data Analysis

### EIA State Electricity Profiles

#### Question 2: Five States with the Dirtiest Electricity Mix
```{r}
library(gt)

dirtiest_states <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  arrange(desc(CO2_MWh)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  select(
    state,
    abbreviation,
    CO2_MWh,
    primary_source,
    electricity_price_MWh
  )

dirtiest_states |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    state = "State",
    abbreviation = "Abbreviation",
    CO2_MWh = "CO2 per MWh",
    primary_source = "Primary Energy Source",
    electricity_price_MWh = "Electricity Price per MWh"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(CO2_MWh, electricity_price_MWh),
    decimals = 2,
    use_seps = TRUE
  ) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Five States with the Dirtiest Electricity Mix"
  )
```
West Virginia is ranked to have the most polluted electrical power among the states shown, having the greatest CO2 emission rate per MWh. The use of coal is the main source of energy for the four states of the five, whereas the exception is Hawaii which uses petroleum.

#### Question 5: New York vs. Texas Electricity Mix
```{r}
ny_tx_cleaner <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  filter(state %in% c("New York", "Texas")) |>
  select(state, CO2_MWh) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = state,
    values_from = CO2_MWh
  ) |>
  mutate(
    times_cleaner = Texas / `New York`
  ) |>
  pull(times_cleaner)

ny_tx_cleaner
```
Based on CO2 emissions per MWh, the electricity mix in New York is `r round(ny_tx_cleaner, 2)` times cleaner compared to that of Texas.

### NTD Energy Usage

#### Question 1: Transit Agencies Using the Most Fuel
```{r}
library(gt)

top_fuel_agencies <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  group_by(`Agency Name`) |>
  summarise(
    across(starts_with("Gallons of"), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    total_gallons = rowSums(across(starts_with("Gallons of")))
  ) |>
  slice_max(
    order_by = total_gallons,
    n = 5,
    with_ties = FALSE
  )

top_fuel_table <- top_fuel_agencies |>
  select(
    `Agency Name`,
    total_gallons,
    `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`,
    `Gallons of Diesel Fuel`,
    `Gallons of Gasoline`
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    `Agency Name` = "Transit Agency",
    total_gallons = "Total Gallons",
    `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas` = "CNG Gallons",
    `Gallons of Diesel Fuel` = "Diesel Gallons",
    `Gallons of Gasoline` = "Gasoline Gallons"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = where(is.numeric),
    decimals = 0,
    use_seps = TRUE
  ) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Five Transit Agencies Using the Most Fuel"
  )

top_fuel_table
```
New Jersey Transit Corporation used the highest quantity of fuel total among the five agencies presented in the discussion, closely followed by the MTA New York City Transit agency. Diesel has comprised a lot of the fuel used by some of these agencies in the name of fuel while the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority has been using compressed natural gas technology.

#### Question 2: Fuel Use Across U.S. Public Transit
```{r}
fuel_totals <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      starts_with("Gallons of"),
      starts_with("Kilowatt hours of")
    ),
    names_to = "fuel_type",
    values_to = "amount"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    unit = if_else(
      str_starts(fuel_type, "Kilowatt hours"),
      "Kilowatt-hours",
      "Gallons"
    ),
    fuel_type = str_remove(
      fuel_type,
      "^(Gallons of |Kilowatt hours of )"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(unit, fuel_type) |>
  summarise(
    total_amount = sum(amount, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(total_amount > 0)

fuel_totals |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = reorder(fuel_type, total_amount),
    y = total_amount
  )) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~unit, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Energy and Fuel Use Across U.S. Public Transit",
    x = "Fuel or Energy Type",
    y = "Total Amount Used"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
There are various forms of energy used by public transportation. For those energy forms which are expressed in terms of gallons, diesel is the most consumed form of fuel. On the other hand, electric propulsion is the form of energy that is most consumed when energy forms are expressed in kilowatt-hours.

#### Question 3: Least Commonly Used Transit Fuel Source
```{r}
fuel_usage_counts <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      starts_with("Gallons of"),
      starts_with("Kilowatt hours of")
    ),
    names_to = "fuel_type",
    values_to = "amount"
  ) |>
  group_by(fuel_type) |>
  summarise(
    services_using = sum(amount > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>

least_used_fuel <- fuel_usage_counts |>
  filter(services_using > 0) |>
  slice_head(n = 1)

least_used_fuel
```
`r least_used_fuel$fuel_type` is the transit fuel that is most uncommonly used because it is used by `r least_used_fuel$services_using` transit service in the dataset.

```{r}
nyc_longest_trip <- NTD_SERVICE |>
```

The NYC transit service with the longest average trip length is `r nyc_longest_trip$AGENCY`'s `r nyc_longest_trip$mode` service in `r nyc_longest_trip$city`, with an average trip length of `r round(nyc_longest_trip$avg_trip_length, 2)` miles.

#### Question 4: Five States with the Fewest Public Transit Passenger Miles
```{r}
fewest_state_miles <- NTD_SERVICE |>
```

Among the five states with the lowest total public transit passenger miles, the state of South Dakota had the least passenger miles. After South Dakota were New Hampshire and North Dakota. ## Emissions Analysis

### Task 5: Calculate Transit Emissions
```{r}
emissions_data <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(
    NTD_ID_num = as.numeric(`NTD ID`)
  ) |>
  left_join(
    NTD_SERVICE |>
      mutate(
        NTD_ID_num = readr::parse_number(NTD_ID)
      ) |>
      select(
        NTD_ID_num,
        mode,
        state
      ) |>
      distinct(),
    by = c(
      "NTD_ID_num",
      "Mode" = "mode"
    )
  ) |>
  left_join(
    EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
      select(
        abbreviation,
        CO2_MWh
      ),
    by = c("state" = "abbreviation")
  )

glimpse(emissions_data)

emissions_data |>
  summarise(
    total_rows = n(),
    missing_state = sum(is.na(state)),
    missing_CO2 = sum(is.na(CO2_MWh))
  )

emissions_data |>
  filter(is.na(CO2_MWh)) |>
  count(state, sort = TRUE)

emissions_complete <- emissions_data |>
  filter(!is.na(CO2_MWh))

dim(emissions_complete)
```
```{r}
emissions_complete <- emissions_complete |>
  mutate(
    # Liquid fossil fuels
    diesel_emissions =
      `Gallons of Diesel Fuel` * 22.45,

    gasoline_emissions =
      `Gallons of Gasoline` * 18.73,

    bunker_emissions =
      `Gallons of Bunker Fuel` * 24.78,

    kerosene_emissions =
      `Gallons of Kerosene` * 21.78,

    lpg_emissions =
      `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas` * 12.68,

    # CNG: retain our gallon-equivalent approximation
    cng_emissions =
      `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas` * 14.43,

    # Electricity: convert kWh to MWh, then multiply by state CO2/MWh
    electric_battery_emissions =
      (`Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery` / 1000) * CO2_MWh,

    electric_propulsion_emissions =
      (`Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion` / 1000) * CO2_MWh,

    # Hydrogen produces no direct CO2 at point of use
    hydrogen_emissions =
      `Kilograms of Hydrogen` * 0,

    # Biofuels treated separately as zero fossil CO2 for this calculation
    biodiesel_emissions =
      `Gallons of Bio-Diesel` * 0,

    ethanol_emissions =
      `Gallons of Ethanol` * 0,

    total_emissions =
      diesel_emissions +
      gasoline_emissions +
      bunker_emissions +
      kerosene_emissions +
      lpg_emissions +
      cng_emissions +
      electric_battery_emissions +
      electric_propulsion_emissions +
      hydrogen_emissions +
      biodiesel_emissions +
      ethanol_emissions
  )

emissions_complete |>
  select(
    `Agency Name`,
    Mode,
    state,
    total_emissions
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(total_emissions)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)
```
After joining the NTD service, NTD energy, and EIA electricity data, the total emissions of carbon dioxide were estimated for each transit agency and mode of transport. From the results, it can be observed that large transit agencies can have high levels of total emissions since they work at a much larger scale and transport many more people.

### Task 6: Normalize Emissions to Transit Usage
```{r}
agency_emissions <- emissions_complete |>
  group_by(NTD_ID_num, `Agency Name`, state) |>
  summarise(
    total_emissions = sum(total_emissions, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

agency_service <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  mutate(
    NTD_ID_num = readr::parse_number(NTD_ID)
  ) |>
  group_by(NTD_ID_num, AGENCY) |>
  summarise(
    total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_passenger_miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

agency_efficiency <- agency_emissions |>
  left_join(
    agency_service,
    by = c(
      "NTD_ID_num",
      "Agency Name" = "AGENCY"
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    emissions_per_upt = total_emissions / total_upt,
    emissions_per_passenger_mile =
      total_emissions / total_passenger_miles
  )

agency_efficiency |>
  select(
    `Agency Name`,
    state,
    total_emissions,
    total_upt,
    total_passenger_miles,
    emissions_per_upt,
    emissions_per_passenger_mile
  ) |>
  arrange(emissions_per_passenger_mile) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)
```
To guarantee comparability between agencies, the total emissions were divided by the number of unlinked passenger trips and passenger miles.

## Green Transit Awards

### Award 1: Greenest Transit Agency
```{r}
greenest_agency <- agency_efficiency |>
  filter(
    total_upt >= 1000000,
    total_passenger_miles > 0,
    is.finite(emissions_per_passenger_mile)
  ) |>
  arrange(emissions_per_passenger_mile) |>
  slice_head(n = 1)

greenest_agency
```
The University of Minnesota was found to be the greenest transit agency amongst all transit agencies having a minimum of one million trips annually since it had the lowest estimated CO2 emissions per passenger mile.

### Award 2: Most Electrified Transit Agency
```{r}
electric_modes <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(
    NTD_ID_num = as.numeric(`NTD ID`),
    electric_mode =
      `Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery` > 0 |
      `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion` > 0
  ) |>
  select(
    NTD_ID_num,
    Mode,
    `Agency Name`,
    electric_mode
  )

electrification_award <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  mutate(
    NTD_ID_num = readr::parse_number(NTD_ID)
  ) |>
  left_join(
    electric_modes,
    by = c(
      "NTD_ID_num",
      "mode" = "Mode",
      "AGENCY" = "Agency Name"
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    electric_mode = replace_na(electric_mode, FALSE)
  ) |>
  group_by(NTD_ID_num, AGENCY) |>
  summarise(
    total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    electric_upt = sum(total_upt[electric_mode], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(total_upt >= 1000000) |>
  mutate(
    electrification_share = electric_upt / total_upt
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(electrification_share)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

electrification_award

electrification_award |>
  select(
    AGENCY,
    total_upt,
    electric_upt,
    electrification_share
  ) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

most_electrified <- electrification_award |>
  filter(electrification_share == max(electrification_share, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(desc(total_upt)) |>
  slice_head(n = 1)

most_electrified
```
The New Jersey Transit Corporation was honored with the Most Electrified Transit Agency award since 100% of their trips reported were made using transit modes using electric power. All transit agencies have reported to 100% usage, New Jersey Transit Corporation had the maximum ridership.


### Green Transit Awards Honor Leaders of Environmental Public Transport

The Green Transit Awards identifies the public transportation organizations within the United States that excel in their environmental performance as well as innovative transport technologies. Using information from the National Transit Database and U.S. Energy Information Administration, the transit agencies were compared using estimates of CO2 emissions, ridership, and electric transport modes.

The winner of the **Greenest Transit Agency Award** is **University of Minnesota**. This award has been given after considering the estimates of the carbon dioxide emissions per passenger mile of the transit agencies having at least one million unlinked passenger trips annually. University of Minnesota has been estimated to emit about `r round(greenest_winner_value, 3)` pounds of CO2 per passenger mile, compared to the median of 0.795 pounds of CO₂ per passenger mile. This means that the University of Minnesota is the most emission-efficient agency as far as CO2 is concerned.

The **Largest Fully Electrified Transit System Award** is awarded to **New Jersey Transit Corporation**. The first criteria of identifying agencies as being fully electrified was that all of the passenger trips reported by them involved transit systems using electric power. Among those agencies that qualified as fully electrified, New Jersey Transit was the one that served the highest number of passengers annually, which was approximately `r scales::comma(fully_electric_winner_value)`. In comparison, the median number of trips made by fully electrified agencies was around `r scales::comma(round(fully_electric_reference))`.

All of the awards taken together illustrate that there are different ways to measure the environmental performance of a company. There are some examples of transit systems that excel through emitting a small amount of pollution compared to the service they offer, while others excel through their capacity to run a system through electric transport means.
